overview.text: The Striped Whipsnake is a fast, alert, non-venomous snake of the western United States and northern Mexico.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: From south-central Washington through the Great Basin to Arizona, New Mexico and western Texas, and northern Mexico.

habitat.text: Shrubland, grassland, sagebrush flats, canyons, piñon-juniper woodland and open pine-oak forest, often near rocky streams.

behaviour.text: Active by day and very quick. It shelters in rock outcrops, burrows, trees and shrubs, and hunts lizards and other animals.

reproduction.text: Lays 3 to 12 eggs in June or July.

recognise.text: Slender and fast with long stripes.
